llm.summary: The skill is aimed at a legitimate UI enhancement, but it asks to patch a local OpenClaw install while the installer and browser script it describes are missing from this ClawHub artifact.

dimensions.detail: The requested Bash/Read/Write authority and PowerShell install flow are proportionate only if the missing patch script exists and enforces the documented target-path limits; without it, the high-impact local modification path is under-supported by the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README instruct running scripts/pcl-patch.ps1 and copying scripts/pcl-model-picker.v8.js, but the inspected artifact contains no scripts directory or enhancement asset, so the claimed implementation and safeguards cannot be verified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documented runtime scope is bounded to index.html, a versioned asset, same-origin update polling, localStorage for picker size, and removal of old matching assets; these are disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The ClawHub artifact discloses a persistent local index.html script tag and browser self-update polling; the scheduled Windows watchdog is described as GitHub-only and was not present in this artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: improve the OpenClaw Control UI model picker by injecting a browser-side enhancement, hiding an account row, and restoring the stock UI on uninstall.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to modify your local OpenClaw Control UI files. Before running anything, verify that the package you use actually includes the patch script and browser asset, inspect those files, and confirm the target OpenClaw dist path. Treat the optional GitHub watchdog as a separate persistence feature that should require explicit consent.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The self-update and watchdog text in CHANGELOG.md describes purpose-aligned repair/reload behavior for a UI patch; the scheduled watchdog is explicitly documented as GitHub-only and not included here, but the missing installer prevents verification of actual behavior.
[AE4] expected: README.md and SPONSORS.md use multilingual Unicode content and payment QR references; inspection did not show prompt-injection instructions, credentials, or hidden execution behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese usage text suggests a broad natural-language install request, but it still names OpenClaw and ModelSelectorOpenClaw; the more important concern is that the local patch command references missing scripts.
[SQP-3] expected: The license and sponsor files contain language/locale statements and multilingual support text; these do not materially affect security risk for this skill.
